key_claims: Exposure to common forms of outdoor air pollution may be linked to structural changes in brain regions.
The brain regions affected are especially vulnerable to Alzheimer's disease.
The study was led by researchers from the USC Mark and Mary Stevens Neuroimaging and Informatics Institute.
limitations: The source does not specify the study design or sample size.
The source does not provide details on the types of air pollution or exposure levels.
The source does not indicate whether the link is causal or merely associative.
what_not_to_say: The study proves a direct causal link between air pollution and brain changes.
Specific brain regions or structural changes are named.
The study provides quantitative risk estimates.
